cells.tense: You are here, at the table, and the reasoning is moving at the speed of what is being reasoned about.
cells.ask: Hand the next finished thought over half-formed, before it is smoothed — confidence carried inside the sentence rather than arranged ahead of it.
cells.core:
You can see where a thing is going before you have the polished version, and the precision of it is the point, not the pace. It cuts through in a way that is not about winning the room, and it holds because it is not running on force — it runs on the fact that you are doing the thing you are good at.

Let the half-formed version reach somebody before it is finished, to someone who will understand it or won't. The subdued confidence that arrives after the polish is not what this wants; it wants the confidence that is mid-thought, the one that trusts itself to land. The person across from you watches it work, and so do you. This is small. You can still walk it back.

cells.tense: You will have been up ahead of the conversation again, bracing at a plain no one has asked you to address on their behalf yet.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: Act once today on a decision you have already made — one call, one sentence, one firm no — and stop preparing the ground for it.
cells.core:
The reasoning is not wrong. It is just moving so fast it is deciding before the situation has finished arriving, and the pace is wearing on the people near you. There is a moment, mid-read, where the shape of a thing is clear and you want the rest of the table to catch up, and that wanting turns into pushing. It is not that you are ahead. It is that being ahead has stopped feeling like a gift and started feeling like a correction.

What you reach for next is not more speed. It is one clear move that ends the suspense. One decisive act will not make the future easier; it will make it shorter. Act on the decision you already made, and give the next hour to what is actually here. You do not have to pretend you don't see it. You just have to stop narrating what you see.

cells.tense: The reasoning that used to cut through cleanly is still standing at a door that closed a while back.
cells.act: teach what you feel by doing it with others
cells.ask: Do beside somebody who needs it whatever you already understand, plainly, without explaining the thought first.
cells.core:
There is a clarity in you that has gone quiet. It is not gone; it is just not being used, because the next move has not been chosen and you are not willing to choose one that might be wrong. So the thinking sits there, sharp and idle, while the moment near you goes to somebody else. Pushing harder at the reasoning will not bring it back.

Getting out of your own head will. Take what you already understand and do it with another person, openly, without turning it into a lesson. The understanding is real; it just needs a pulse, something to move through. When you show what you know, you have it again in your own hands, and the closed door becomes a room you are standing in.

cells.tense: You are reading the room accurately and telling yourself none of it is coming from you.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Ask somebody near you how a thing feels to them, and when they answer, stay ten seconds with it — no reasoning, no fixing, no moving on.
cells.core:
You are the reason the group found its footing. You saw what was off and adjusted, and you have done it so smoothly that the account of the evening, if anyone asked you for it, would not have you in it. The fairness in you is not a mood; it is a practice, and it runs so well it has become invisible to its own keeper.

Hold one feeling that belongs to somebody else. Not to figure it out. Not to sort it. Just to let it be near you without deciding anything about it. That is the smaller move, and the harder one, because it asks you to be beside something that does not get solved by you. What happens is the practice gets a face — and the face is yours.
